\caption{The trade-off from a lower marginal top applicant, holding $OC$ fixed. In each panel the marginal top applicant falls from $\hat{\theta}^T_H$ to $\hat{\theta}^T_L$, so winning probabilities rise from the solid to the dotted curve. Green is the intensive margin (applicants above $\hat{\theta}^T_H$ win more often); red is the extensive margin (the entrants win less often than the previous average $\mathcal{T}(\hat{\theta}^T_H)$, dashed). The average acceptance rate moves to the dotted level, rising in (a) and falling in (b). The horizontal axis is the merit quantile $G(\theta)$, so the shaded areas are exactly the gain and loss for any $G$. (a) $G$ uniform on $[-1.6,1.6]$, with strictly decreasing Mills ratio; (b) $G$ Lomax with shape $1.2$ and scale $2$ on $[-1.6,\infty)$, whose Mills ratio is increasing. $F$ standard normal, $\sigma=2$, $v^T=1$, $OC=0.3$; in both panels $\hat{\theta}^T_H$ and $\hat{\theta}^T_L$ are the $37.5$th and $18.75$th percentiles of merit. $\mathcal{T}(\cdot)$ suppresses the fixed arguments $\sigma$ and $OC$.}
\label{fig:toptrade}
\end{figure}
